maml:description.maml:para: Establish authenticated connections to one or more Microsoft cloud services.

1. Checks whether an existing connection is already present and optionally re-uses it, prompting for confirmation unless DontConfirm is set.
2. Disconnects and reconnects when the existing connection is missing required Scopes or when multiple services are connected under different accounts.
3. Verifies after connecting that all services share the same account identity when their definitions are marked as matchable.
When CheckOnly is set the cmdlet only verifies connectivity and throws a terminating error for any service that is not already connected.
Pre-acquired access token for token-based authentication; bypasses the interactive login flow when provided.

When present, skips the interactive confirmation prompt when a service is already connected.

Windows-only; on non-Windows platforms the check is silently skipped. Counterpart to Invoke-EnsureAdministrator: use this where a script must not run elevated. A or from the P/Invoke elevation query is treated as an indeterminate soft-pass.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Throws a terminating PermissionDenied error when the session is elevated.

maml:description.maml:para: Writes a message to the host at the Error level, or throws a terminating error.
When -Throw is set the message is wrapped in an and passed to ThrowTerminatingError. Otherwise the message is suppressed when $ErrorActionPreference is SilentlyContinue or Ignore.
The caller's used as the error target when throwing; resolved from the call stack when omitted.
The on whose behalf ThrowTerminatingError is called; defaults to this cmdlet.
The to assign when -Throw is used; defaults to NotSpecified.
Hashtable of parameters to splat into the cmdlet; when provided, all other parameters are ignored.
The error message text to write or throw.
When set, returns the formatted string to the pipeline instead of writing it to the host.
When set, throws a terminating error instead of writing the message to the host.
Unicode prefix to prepend to the message; defaults to ❌ when omitted.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Throws a terminating error with the ObjectNotFound category.

maml:description.maml:para: Runs exit handlers and terminates the pipeline with a non-zero exit code.

Looks up the registered description for and writes it as an error display message. If an is supplied the deepest exception message is also shown. All registered exit handlers are executed before the terminating error is thrown. Pass to suppress the terminating error (useful in tests).
Suppress the terminating error after running handlers; the cmdlet returns normally instead.
The error record that caused the exit; its deepest exception message is displayed.
The numeric exit code to return to the caller.
Format arguments applied to the registered exit-code description string via string.Format.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Displays the description registered for exit code 1, runs all exit handlers, then throws a terminating error carrying exit code 1.

maml:description.maml:para: Runs all registered exit handlers for the current runspace.
Iterates every handler registered via Register-ExitHandler. Handlers marked OnlyFailure are skipped unless is set. Debug and warning messages produced by handlers are forwarded to the calling stream.
Indicate that the current exit is a failure, enabling handlers registered with -OnlyFailure.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Runs all exit handlers, including those registered with
-OnlyFailure

maml:description.maml:para: Writes a message to the host at the Information level.
Suppressed when $InformationPreference is Ignore. Accepts either individual parameters (Splat set) or a pre-built hashtable (InputObject set).
Hashtable of parameters to splat into the cmdlet; when provided, all other parameters are ignored.
The message text to write to the host.
When set, returns the formatted string to the pipeline instead of writing it to the host.
Unicode prefix to prepend to the message; defaults to ℹ️ when omitted.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Writes the message in cyan with the info prefix if InformationPreference allows it.

maml:description.maml:para: Runs a script block against each local user's registry hive.

Enumerates all user profiles under HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ProfileList (filtering to standard and AzureAD SIDs). For each profile, temporarily loads the ntuser.dat hive via reg.exe if it is not already mounted, invokes the script block, then unloads the hive if it was loaded by this cmdlet. The script block receives a PSObject with SID, UserHive, and Username properties. Only supported on Windows.
Script block to execute for each user profile; receives a PSObject with SID, UserHive, and Username.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Writes a DWord registry value to every loaded user hive.

maml:description.maml:para: Iterates a collection with a progress bar, invoking a scriptblock for each item.

Items are retrieved via the Get scriptblock, then each item is passed to Process. Progress is reported as a percentage; the bar is completed and dismissed when all items finish. If an item throws, FailedProcessItem is called when provided; otherwise the item is collected and a warning is emitted after the loop.
Activity label displayed in the progress bar header; defaults to "Main" when omitted.
ScriptBlock invoked when Process throws for an item; when omitted, the item is added to a failed-items list and a warning is emitted.
ScriptBlock that returns a display name for an item; falls back to ToString() when omitted.
ScriptBlock that returns the collection of items to iterate.
Progress bar ID used to stack multiple concurrent progress bars; defaults to 0.
ScriptBlock invoked for each item; receives the item as the first positional argument.
Format template for the progress status line. Placeholders: {0} = completion percentage, {1} = current index, {2} = total count. Defaults to "Processing [item]..." when omitted.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Removes each file under C:\ with a live progress bar.

maml:description.maml:para: Runs exit handlers and terminates the pipeline with a success exit code.

Executes all registered exit handlers (non-failure mode) and then throws a terminating error with the identifier QuickExit. Use this when a script should stop cleanly without indicating a failure condition.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Runs all non-failure exit handlers then terminates the pipeline immediately.

maml:description.maml:para: Run a script's main entry-point block with lifecycle management, restart support, and exit-code handling.

Applies Set-StrictMode -Version 3 and prints a legal disclaimer before invoking , unless suppressed via or . Handles the QuickExit, FailedExit, and RestartScript control-flow error signals, and always invokes registered exit handlers when the run loop terminates. Bound parameters from the calling are splatted onto .
Calling cmdlet context; its bound parameters are splatted onto .
When set, suppresses the legal disclaimer message printed before Main runs.
Script block executed as the script's entry point.
When set, skips applying Set-StrictMode -Version 3 to the runspace before Main runs.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Runs the script block as the script entry point with strict mode and the disclaimer enabled.

maml:description.maml:para: Displays a countdown progress bar for a fixed duration, then invokes a callback.
The progress bar ticks approximately every 50 ms. If -AllowCancel is set and a key is pressed before the timeout elapses, CancelScript is invoked instead of TimeoutScript.
Activity label shown in the progress bar header.
When set, the user can press any key to cancel the countdown and invoke CancelScript.
ScriptBlock invoked when the user cancels before the timeout elapses.
Format string for the progress status; {0} is replaced with the whole seconds remaining.
Timeout duration in seconds.
ScriptBlock invoked when the timeout elapses without cancellation.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Counts down 10 seconds, then restarts the computer.

maml:description.maml:para: Acquires an exclusive file lock, executes a script block, then releases the lock.

Derives the script name from the caller, builds the lock path, and waits for the lock before invoking . The lock is always released in a finally block, so it is safe even when the script block throws. Pipeline output from the script block is forwarded to the caller.
Optional arguments splatted to the script block when it is invoked.
Resource identifier used to construct the lock file name.
The script block to execute while holding the lock.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Runs driver installation exclusively, preventing concurrent runs for the same resource.

maml:description.maml:para: Writes a message to the host at the Verbose level.
Suppressed when $VerbosePreference is SilentlyContinue or Ignore. Accepts either individual parameters (Splat set) or a pre-built hashtable (InputObject set).
Hashtable of parameters to splat into the cmdlet; when provided, all other parameters are ignored.
The message text to write to the host.
When set, returns the formatted string to the pipeline instead of writing it to the host.
Unicode prefix to prepend to the message; defaults to 🔍 when omitted.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Writes the message in yellow with the verbose prefix if VerbosePreference allows it.

maml:description.maml:para: Writes a message to the host at the Warning level.
Suppressed when $WarningPreference is SilentlyContinue or Ignore. Accepts either individual parameters (Splat set) or a pre-built hashtable (InputObject set).
Hashtable of parameters to splat into the cmdlet; when provided, all other parameters are ignored.
The message text to write to the host.
When set, returns the formatted string to the pipeline instead of writing it to the host.
Unicode prefix to prepend to the message; defaults to ⚠️ when omitted.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Writes the message in yellow with the warning prefix if WarningPreference allows it.

maml:description.maml:para: Runs a script block inside a newly created ephemeral temporary folder.

Creates a unique temp folder, sets it as the working directory, invokes the script block, then restores the original location and deletes the folder (best-effort) on completion regardless of whether the script block throws.
Script block to execute inside the ephemeral folder; runs with the folder as the current working directory.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Downloads and extracts a file into a temp folder that is deleted afterwards.

maml:description.maml:para: Writes a formatted, coloured message to the host or returns it as a string.

This is the low-level write helper used by all level-specific cmdlets. When ShouldWrite is false the call is a no-op. When PassThru is set the formatted string is returned to the pipeline instead. An optional InformationTag is attached when writing to the information stream.
Optional tag attached to the information stream record, used to filter output downstream.
Hashtable of parameters to splat into the cmdlet; when provided, all other parameters are ignored.
Number of spaces to indent continuation lines of a multi-line message.
When set, returns the formatted string to the pipeline instead of writing it to the host.
Console colour name for the message text (e.g., "Cyan", "Red").
The message text to format and write.
Optional Unicode prefix (e.g., an emoji) to prepend to the message.
When explicitly false, suppresses all output; null or true allows writing.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Writes "Done" in green to the console.
Returns the formatted string via the pipeline.

maml:description.maml:para: Register a CLR type as a dispatchable event in the event store.
Creates an empty for the given type. Must be called before Register-EventSubscription or Submit-Event can be used with that type.
CLR type to register as a dispatchable event.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Registers MyEvent so that subscriptions and dispatches can target it.

maml:description.maml:para: Subscribe a script block to a registered event type, returning the subscription GUID.

The event type must have been registered with Register-Event before subscribing. Callbacks are invoked in order (High before Normal before Low); within the same priority, dispatch order is deterministic by subscription GUID.
Script block invoked when an event of is dispatched; receives the event instance as its first argument.
CLR type whose event this callback subscribes to; must already be registered via Register-Event.
Dispatch priority relative to other subscribers for the same event type; defaults to .

dev:remarks.maml:para: Subscribes to MyEvent and stores the GUID for later removal.

maml:description.maml:para: Registers a human-readable description for a new exit code and returns the assigned code.

Each call allocates the next sequential exit code for the current runspace and stores the supplied description. The description is later retrieved by Invoke-FailedExit to display a meaningful message. Exit codes are runspace-scoped and not shared across sessions.
Human-readable description shown when this exit code is used with Invoke-FailedExit.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Registers the description and assigns an integer exit code, returned to
$exitCode

maml:description.maml:para: Registers a script block to run when the script exits.

Handlers are stored per-runspace and executed in registration order by Invoke-Handlers and Invoke-FailedExit. Re-registering a handler with the same name overwrites the previous entry with a warning. Use to restrict a handler to failure exits only.
The script block to execute when the script exits.
Unique name for this handler; re-using an existing name overwrites the prior registration.
Restrict this handler to failure exits; skip it when exiting successfully.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Registers a cleanup handler that runs on every exit.

maml:description.maml:para: Releases a lock file handle and removes the lock file from disk.
Safely closes the and deletes the file at . Both parameters are optional; null values are handled gracefully. Prefer Invoke-UnderLock for automatic acquisition and release.
The file handle returned by Wait-LockFile; closed if non-null.
Full path to the lock file to delete; skipped if null or already absent.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Closes the handle and deletes the lock file.

maml:description.maml:para: Strips the byte-order mark (BOM) from a byte array for the given encoding.
Returns the input byte array unchanged when no BOM is present.
The byte array to strip the BOM from.
The encoding whose BOM prefix to remove.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Returns $bytes with the UTF-8 BOM removed if present.

maml:description.maml:para: Removes a user from a local group via the ADSI WinNT provider.
Returns when the user was removed, or when the user was not a member of the group. Only works on Windows via the WinNT ADSI provider.
The group to remove the member from; accepts an AdsiPrincipal or a group name string.
The user to remove from the group; accepts an AdsiPrincipal or a user name string.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Removes the local user localadmin from the Administrators group.

maml:description.maml:para: Removes a registry value if it exists.
No-ops silently if the registry path or the named value does not exist. Uses ShouldProcess to support -WhatIf and -Confirm. Only supported on Windows.
The name of the registry value to remove.
The registry path to the key container (e.g., HKLM:\SOFTWARE\MyApp).

dev:remarks.maml:para: Deletes the OldSetting value from HKLM:\SOFTWARE\MyApp.

maml:description.maml:para: Runs exit handlers and signals the host to restart the current script.

Executes all registered exit handlers (non-failure mode), writes an informational restart message, then throws a terminating error with identifier RestartScript. The calling harness is responsible for catching this error and re-launching the script.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Runs all non-failure exit handlers then signals a restart.

maml:description.maml:para: Defines a read-only script variable whose value is computed lazily on first access.
The variable is set in the caller's local scope as read-only. The first time it is read, the Value script block executes and the result is memoised. Also available as the alias lazy.
The variable name to create in the caller's local scope.
When set, emits the generated lazy script block to the pipeline.
Script block invoked on first access to compute the variable's value.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Creates a lazy $Config variable that loads the config file on first use.
Same as above using the lazy alias.

maml:description.maml:para: Creates or updates a registry value, creating intermediate key nodes as needed.

If the target value already exists it is updated in place; otherwise a new value is created with the specified type. All intermediate registry path segments are created if absent. Uses ShouldProcess to support -WhatIf and -Confirm. Only supported on Windows.
The name of the registry value to create or update.
The registry value type (e.g., DWord, String, ExpandString).
The registry path to the key container (e.g., HKLM:\SOFTWARE\MyApp).
The data to write to the registry value.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Creates or updates the Enabled DWord value under HKLM:\SOFTWARE\MyApp.

maml:description.maml:para: Starts a PowerShell script block asynchronously and returns an AsyncTaskRun token.
Launches the script in a new PowerShell runspace using BeginInvoke. The returned AsyncTaskRun can be passed to Wait-Task to collect the result. Also available as the alias async.
Optional pipeline input attached to the AsyncTaskRun token for correlation.
The script block to execute asynchronously in a new PowerShell runspace.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Starts the script asynchronously and stores the run token.
Same as above using the async alias.

maml:description.maml:para: Dispatch an event instance to all subscribers registered for its runtime type.
The runtime type of determines which EventRegistration is looked up. wrappers are unwrapped before dispatch. Silently no-ops when no registration exists for the type.
Event object to dispatch; its runtime type must match a type registered via Register-Event.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Dispatches a MyEvent instance to all currently registered subscribers.

maml:description.maml:para: Forces a W32TM time resynchronisation if the last sync exceeds the threshold age.

Checks the age of the last successful sync via Get-LastSyncTime. Returns when a resync was triggered and succeeded, when the existing sync time is within the threshold. Windows-only; requires the w32tm service to be running.
Maximum allowed age of the last sync before a resync is triggered; defaults to 7 days.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Resyncs the clock if the last sync was more than 7 days ago.
Resyncs the clock if the last sync was more than 1 hour ago.

maml:description.maml:para: Return when the current session is hosted inside the N-able fmplugin.exe process.
Inspects the console window-title leaf and compares it case-insensitively to fmplugin.exe. Use this to suppress UI-heavy output paths that do not render correctly inside the N-able runner.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Conditionally adjusts output based on the detected host environment.

maml:description.maml:para: Tests whether the current process is running as the NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM account.
Returns on non-Windows platforms without throwing.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Returns $true when the PowerShell host is running as SYSTEM.

maml:description.maml:para: Tests whether the current operating system is Windows 11 or later.
Returns on non-Windows platforms without throwing. Detects Windows 11 by OS description string or build number >= 22000.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Returns $true when running on Windows 11 or later.

maml:description.maml:para: Tests whether a package is installed via the detected package manager.
Detects the available package manager and queries it for the named package. Returns if the package is installed, otherwise.
The name of the package to test for installation.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Returns $true if git is installed, $false otherwise.

maml:description.maml:para: Tests whether a user is a member of a local group via the ADSI WinNT provider.
Returns when the user is a direct member of the group, otherwise . Only works on Windows via the WinNT ADSI provider.
The group to test membership against; accepts an AdsiPrincipal or a group name string.
The user to test; accepts an AdsiPrincipal or a user name string.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Returns $true if localadmin is a member of the Administrators group.

maml:description.maml:para: Tests whether any network interface with internet connectivity is available.
Inspects local network interfaces for an operational adapter that is internet-capable. Returns when such an interface exists, otherwise .

dev:remarks.maml:para: Returns $true if at least one internet-capable network interface is up.

maml:description.maml:para: Tests whether all parameters in a script block are declared with types from the allowed set.
Statically analyses the param block of the input script to verify that every parameter type name is present in ValidTypes.
The script block, file path, or Ast node whose parameters are validated.
The set of type name strings that parameters are permitted to use.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Returns $true because the parameter is typed as string.

maml:description.maml:para: Returns if a registry value exists, otherwise.
Returns if the registry path itself does not exist. Only supported on Windows.
The name of the registry value to test for existence.
The registry path to the key container (e.g., HKLM:\SOFTWARE\MyApp).

dev:remarks.maml:para: Returns $true if the Enabled value is present under HKLM:\SOFTWARE\MyApp.

maml:description.maml:para: Tests whether a script block's inferred return types are all within the allowed set.
Returns when every inferred return type is contained in ValidTypes, otherwise . When AllowNull is specified, void/null returns do not cause a failure.
When set, allows void/null return types even if they are not in ValidTypes.
The script block, file path, or Ast node whose return types are tested.
The set of .NET types that the script block is allowed to return.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Returns $true because the script block returns string.
Returns $true because null is allowed.

maml:description.maml:para: Uninstalls a package using the detected system package manager.
Detects the available package manager (e.g., Chocolatey, Winget) and removes the named package. Uses ShouldProcess to support -WhatIf and -Confirm. Terminates on failure unless -NoFail is specified.
When set, writes a non-terminating error instead of terminating if uninstallation fails.
The name of the package to uninstall.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Uninstalls the git package using the available package manager.
Attempts uninstallation and writes a non-terminating error if it fails.

maml:description.maml:para: Remove a subscription from a registered event, returning if it was found and removed.
Returns when the event type is not registered, or no subscription with the given GUID exists. Idempotent — calling with an already-removed returns without error.
CLR type whose event registration contains the subscription to remove.
GUID returned by Register-EventSubscription when the subscription was created.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Removes the subscription identified by $subscriptionId from the MyEvent registration.

maml:description.maml:para: Updates a package to its latest version using the detected system package manager.
Detects the available package manager (e.g., Chocolatey, Winget) and updates the named package. Uses ShouldProcess to support -WhatIf and -Confirm. Writes a non-terminating error if the update fails.
The name of the package to update.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Updates the git package to its latest available version.

maml:description.maml:para: Waits for and acquires an exclusive write lock on the specified lock file path.

Polls until the lock is available, up to a 600-second timeout. Writes process metadata (PID, optional owner, timestamp) into the lock file. Returns the open handle; pass it to Release-LockFile when done.
Optional owner name written into the lock file metadata for diagnostics.
Full path to the lock file to acquire.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Acquires the lock and returns the file handle.

maml:description.maml:para: Waits for one or more AsyncTaskRun or Task objects to complete and emits their results.

Collects all piped run objects in ProcessRecord, then blocks in EndProcessing until each completes. By default emits the result value; with PassThru emits the original run or Task object. Also available as the alias await.
When set, emits the original AsyncTaskRun or Task object instead of its result.
An AsyncTaskRun or Task object, or a collection of them, to wait for; accepted from the pipeline.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Starts an async task and waits for the result, returning "hello".
Waits for the task and emits the original AsyncTaskRun object.
